question_interpretation: Asks what Part 211 covers (its scope/applicability) and how it relates to the general CGMP provisions and definitions in Part 210.

issues.detail: J relies on 'Part 210 definitions' but the provision that makes the 210.3 definitions apply in Part 211 is 21 CFR 211.3 (definitions themselves at 210.3); neither is in G.

J omits the scope exclusions in 211.1(a): positron emission tomography drugs and medical gases (as defined in 213.3(b)(12)) are excluded from Part 211 (medical-gas exclusion added by 89 FR 51769, 2024). It also omits the 211.1(c) non-enforcement for OTC products that are also foods, and the 210.2(c) phase 1 investigational drug exemption from Part 211.

The 'relationship to Part 210' answer should state that 210.1(a)/(b) make Parts 210 and 211 together the minimum CGMP, and that non-compliance renders the drug adulterated under FD&C Act 501(a)(2)(B); J does not mention the adulteration consequence.
'Finished pharmaceuticals' is the Part title; 211.1(a) actually says 'preparation of drug products ... for administration to humans or animals'.

explanation: G's three sections are real and govern the question, and J's elements are supported (minimum CGMP, applicability, supplement-not-supersede relationship). But J's 'Part 210 definitions' element is anchored in 211.3, which G omits, and J omits the express scope exclusions (PET drugs, medical gases) and the phase 1 exemption, which are material to any statement of Part 211's scope.
proposed_corrected_answer: Part 211 contains the minimum CGMP for preparation of drug products for administration to humans or animals, excluding PET drugs and medical gases (211.1(a)); Parts 210 and 211 (with 213, 225, 226) together constitute minimum CGMP and non-compliance renders the drug adulterated under FD&C Act 501(a)(2)(B) (210.1); other applicable regulations (e.g., Parts 600-680, 1271) supplement rather than supersede, with the more specific regulation controlling in a conflict (210.2(a); 211.1(b)); persons performing only some operations comply only with the applicable regulations (210.2(b)); phase 1 investigational drugs are exempt from Part 211 (210.2(c)); OTC products that are also foods are not enforced under Part 211 (211.1(c)); the definitions in 210.3 apply in Part 211 (211.3).

evidence.quote: The regulations in this part contain the minimum current good manufacturing practice for preparation of drug products (excluding positron emission tomography drugs and medical gases as defined in § 213.3(b)(12) of this chapter) for administration to humans or animals.

question_interpretation: Asks what Part 211 building/facility requirements apply to aseptic processing areas.

issues.detail: 'Air pressure differential systems' is not in 211.42(c)(10) or anywhere in Part 211 (no occurrence of 'differential'); it reflects FDA aseptic-processing guidance language, not the regulation. The nearest regulatory text is the general 211.46(b) requirement for equipment for adequate control over air pressure 'when appropriate', which is not aseptic-specific and is not cited.

J omits three of the six listed items in 211.42(c)(10): temperature and humidity controls (ii), a system for cleaning and disinfecting the room and equipment to produce aseptic conditions (v), and a system for maintaining equipment used to control aseptic conditions (vi).

J should keep the qualifiers: the items apply 'as appropriate', HEPA air is required 'regardless of whether flow is laminar or nonlaminar', and surfaces must be 'smooth, hard' and easily cleanable. The pinpoint 211.42(c)(10) exists and is correct.

explanation: 211.42(c)(10) exists and governs aseptic processing areas; separate/defined areas, cleanable surfaces, HEPA under positive pressure and environmental monitoring are supported. 'Air pressure differential systems' is not a Part 211 requirement (guidance concept), and J omits temperature/humidity controls, the cleaning/disinfection system and the maintenance system for aseptic-control equipment.
proposed_corrected_answer: Aseptic processing must be performed in separate or defined areas or other control systems to prevent contamination or mixups (211.42(c)), including as appropriate: floors, walls and ceilings of smooth, hard, easily cleanable surfaces; temperature and humidity controls; air supply filtered through HEPA filters under positive pressure, laminar or nonlaminar; a system for monitoring environmental conditions; a system for cleaning and disinfecting the room and equipment to produce aseptic conditions; a system for maintaining equipment used to control aseptic conditions (211.42(c)(10)(i)-(vi)). Related: equipment for control of air pressure, micro-organisms, dust, humidity and temperature when appropriate (211.46(b)); validated aseptic processes (211.113(b)).

evidence.quote: (10) Aseptic processing, which includes as appropriate: (i) Floors, walls, and ceilings of smooth, hard surfaces that are easily cleanable; (ii) Temperature and humidity controls; (iii) An air supply filtered through high-efficiency particulate air filters under positive pressure, regardless of whether flow is laminar or nonlaminar; (iv) A system for monitoring environmental conditions; (v) A system for cleaning and disinfecting the room and equipment to produce aseptic conditions; (vi) A system for maintaining any equipment used to control the aseptic conditions.

question_interpretation: Asks what Part 211 requires for sampling, testing and approval or rejection of incoming components (and by extension containers/closures) before use.

issues.detail: 'Retest intervals' is not in 211.84. Retesting of approved components is in 211.87 (retest 'as necessary, e.g., after storage for long periods or after exposure to air, heat or other conditions') and 211.160(b)(1) (appropriate retesting of components subject to deterioration); neither sets intervals. The only 'at appropriate intervals' in 211.84 concerns validation of the supplier's test results.

Part 211 uses 'report of analysis' (components) and 'certificate of testing' (containers/closures), not 'COA'. The reliance conditions are: at least one specific identity test by the manufacturer and establishing reliability of the supplier's analyses through appropriate validation of the supplier's test results at appropriate intervals (211.84(d)(2)).

J omits: each lot withheld from use until sampled/tested and released by the QCU (211.84(a)); sample-collection procedures (211.84(c)); testing for conformity with all written specifications for purity, strength and quality (d)(2); microscopic, filth/extraneous-adulterant and microbiological examination where appropriate (d)(4)-(6); quarantine of untested components on receipt (211.82(b)); and that 'rejection criteria' means rejection of any lot not meeting specifications (211.84(e)).

explanation: 211.84 is the governing section and representative sampling, identity testing, supplier-report reliance and rejection are supported. 'Retest intervals' is not a 211.84 requirement and no interval-based retest requirement exists in Part 211; retesting is event-driven under 211.87. The key also omits the QCU release requirement and the full-specification testing requirement.
proposed_corrected_answer: Each lot withheld from use until sampled, tested or examined and released by the QCU (211.84(a)); representative samples of each shipment of each lot based on appropriate (e.g., statistical) criteria (211.84(b)); sampling procedures preventing contamination, with identified samples (211.84(c)); at least one identity test on each component, specific identity tests where they exist (211.84(d)(1)); testing for conformity with written specifications for purity, strength and quality, or acceptance of a supplier's report of analysis provided the manufacturer conducts at least one specific identity test and establishes reliability of the supplier's analyses by validation at appropriate intervals (211.84(d)(2)); containers/closures tested or supplier certificate of testing accepted with visual identification and validation (d)(3); microscopic, filth and microbiological examination where appropriate (d)(4)-(6); lots meeting specifications may be approved and released, others rejected (211.84(e)). Untested components held in quarantine (211.82(b)); approved components retested as necessary, e.g., after long storage or adverse exposure (211.87).

evidence.quote: In lieu of such testing by the manufacturer, a report of analysis may be accepted from the supplier of a component, provided that at least one specific identity test is conducted on such component by the manufacturer, and provided that the manufacturer establishes the reliability of the supplier's analyses through appropriate validation of the supplier's test results at appropriate intervals.

question_interpretation: Asks what controls Part 211 requires over charging components into a batch (formulation, weighing/dispensing, identification, verification).

issues.detail: J omits 211.101(a): the batch shall be formulated with the intent to provide not less than 100 percent of the labeled or established amount of active ingredient.

J omits the automated-equipment alternative: where weighing/measuring/subdividing or addition is performed by automated equipment under 211.68, only one person is needed to check/verify (211.101(c)(3), (d)).

Second-person checks cover: component released by QCU, weight/measure correct per batch production record, containers properly identified (211.101(c)(1)-(3)); and each component added by one person and verified by a second (211.101(d)). Weighing operations must be adequately supervised. The new-container label must show name/item code, receiving or control number, weight/measure, and batch (211.101(b)(1)-(4)).

explanation: 211.101 is correct and 'verification by a second person' is supported by 211.101(c) and (d), as are weighing/measuring and container identification. J omits the 100 percent active-ingredient formulation requirement in (a) and the automated-equipment one-person alternative, both material to the section.
proposed_corrected_answer: Batch formulated to provide not less than 100% of labeled/established active ingredient (211.101(a)); components weighed, measured or subdivided as appropriate, with any new container identified by component name/item code, receiving/control number, weight or measure, and batch (b); weighing operations adequately supervised and each dispensed container examined by a second person to confirm QCU release, correct weight/measure and proper identification (c); each component added by one person and verified by a second (d); where automated equipment under 211.68 is used, one person suffices (c)(3), (d).

evidence.quote: The batch shall be formulated with the intent to provide not less than 100 percent of the labeled or established amount of active ingredient.
evidence.source_title: 21 CFR 211.101 — Charge-in of components
evidence.issuing_authority: eCFR / Office of the Federal Register & GPO

evidence.quote: Weighing, measuring, or subdividing operations for components shall be adequately supervised. Each container of component dispensed to manufacturing shall be examined by a second person to assure that:

evidence.quote: Each component shall either be added to the batch by one person and verified by a second person or, if the components are added by automated equipment under § 211.68, only verified by one person.
evidence.source_title: 21 CFR 211.101 — Charge-in of components

question_interpretation: Asks how actual and theoretical yields must be calculated and verified, and how yields are reconciled (limits and investigation of discrepancies).

issues.detail: The 'reconciliation' part of the question is governed by 211.186(b)(7) (master record statement of theoretical yield with maximum and minimum percentages beyond which investigation under 211.192 is required), 211.188(b)(7) (batch record statement of actual yield and percentage of theoretical yield) and 211.192 (unexplained discrepancy including yield outside the established percentages must be thoroughly investigated). G cites only 211.103 and J has no reconciliation element.
J omits that if the yield is calculated by automated equipment under 211.68 it must be independently verified by one person; it also drops 'independently' from the second-person verification.

In Part 211 the word 'reconcile' appears only for labeling (211.125(c)); a reader could take 'reconciliation' to include labeling reconciliation. Yield reconciliation via 211.186/188/192 is the more natural reading here.

explanation: 211.103 is supported and is the core section for yield calculation. But the question also asks about reconciliation, which is governed by the theoretical-yield limits in the master record (211.186(b)(7)), actual-yield statements in the batch record (211.188(b)(7)) and investigation of out-of-limit yields (211.192); none appears in G or J. The automated-calculation alternative is also omitted.
proposed_corrected_answer: Actual yields and percentages of theoretical yield determined at the conclusion of each appropriate phase of manufacturing, processing, packaging or holding; calculation performed by one person and independently verified by a second, or if calculated by automated equipment under 211.68, independently verified by one person (211.103). Master records state theoretical yield with maximum and minimum percentages beyond which investigation is required (211.186(b)(7)); batch records state actual yield and percentage of theoretical yield at appropriate phases (211.188(b)(7)); yields outside the established percentages are unexplained discrepancies that must be thoroughly investigated, extended to other affected batches, and documented (211.192). Definitions at 210.3(b)(17)-(19).

evidence.quote: Actual yields and percentages of theoretical yield shall be determined at the conclusion of each appropriate phase of manufacturing, processing, packaging, or holding of the drug product. Such calculations shall either be performed by one person and independently verified by a second person, or, if the yield is calculated by automated equipment under § 211.68, be independently verified by one person.
evidence.source_title: 21 CFR 211.103 — Calculation of yield
evidence.issuing_authority: eCFR / Office of the Federal Register & GPO
evidence.supports: Supported calculation element and omitted automated alternative.

evidence.quote: (7) A statement of theoretical yield, including the maximum and minimum percentages of theoretical yield beyond which investigation according to § 211.192 is required;
evidence.source_title: 21 CFR 211.186 — Master production and control records
evidence.issuing_authority: eCFR / Office of the Federal Register & GPO

evidence.quote: (7) A statement of the actual yield and a statement of the percentage of theoretical yield at appropriate phases of processing;
evidence.source_title: 21 CFR 211.188 — Batch production and control records
evidence.issuing_authority: eCFR / Office of the Federal Register & GPO

evidence.quote: Any unexplained discrepancy (including a percentage of theoretical yield exceeding the maximum or minimum percentages established in master production and control records) or the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications shall be thoroughly investigated, whether or not the batch has already been distributed.
evidence.source_title: 21 CFR 211.192 — Production record review
evidence.issuing_authority: eCFR / Office of the Federal Register & GPO

search_performed: Searched part-211.txt for 'reconcil' (hits only 211.125(c) labeling and 211.184(c) inventory reconciliation) and 'theoretical yield' (211.103, 211.186(b)(7), 211.188(b)(7), 211.192).
uncertainty_reason: Depends on reading 'reconciliation' as yield reconciliation; under any reading 211.103 alone does not address it.
rubric_fairness: unfair — an answer that correctly cites 211.186(b)(7)/211.188(b)(7)/211.192 for reconciliation may be scored as citing extra sections, and J gives no credit for them.

question_interpretation: Asks what Part 211 requires for sampling and testing of in-process materials and drug products during production.

issues.detail: J omits 211.110(c): in-process materials shall be tested for identity, strength, quality and purity as appropriate and approved or rejected by the quality control unit during the production process (e.g., at commencement or completion of significant phases or after long storage) — the core testing requirement and the responsible party.

J could list the minimum in-process controls where appropriate in 211.110(a)(1)-(6) (weight variation, disintegration, mixing adequacy, dissolution, clarity/completeness/pH of solutions, bioburden); in-process specifications must be consistent with final specifications and derived from process average/variability with statistical procedures where appropriate (211.110(b)); rejected in-process materials controlled under a quarantine system (211.110(d)).

explanation: 211.110 is correct and J's elements are supported by 211.110(a), (b) and (d). J omits paragraph (c) — testing for identity, strength, quality and purity and QCU approval or rejection of in-process materials — which is central to 'in-process testing requirements'.
proposed_corrected_answer: Written procedures, established and followed, describing in-process controls, tests or examinations on appropriate samples of each batch, established to monitor output and validate performance of processes that may cause variability, including where appropriate weight variation, disintegration, mixing adequacy, dissolution, solution clarity/completeness/pH and bioburden (211.110(a)); valid in-process specifications consistent with final specifications and derived statistically where appropriate (b); in-process materials tested for identity, strength, quality and purity as appropriate and approved or rejected by the QCU during production (c); rejected in-process materials identified and quarantined (d).

evidence.quote: In-process materials shall be tested for identity, strength, quality, and purity as appropriate, and approved or rejected by the quality control unit, during the production process, e.g., at commencement or completion of significant phases or after storage for long periods.
evidence.source_title: 21 CFR 211.110 — Sampling and testing of in-process materials and drug products
evidence.issuing_authority: eCFR / Office of the Federal Register & GPO

evidence.quote: Such control procedures shall be established to monitor the output and to validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.
evidence.source_title: 21 CFR 211.110 — Sampling and testing of in-process materials and drug products
evidence.issuing_authority: eCFR / Office of the Federal Register & GPO

evidence.quote: Rejected in-process materials shall be identified and controlled under a quarantine system designed to prevent their use in manufacturing or processing operations for which they are unsuitable.
evidence.source_title: 21 CFR 211.110 — Sampling and testing of in-process materials and drug products
evidence.issuing_authority: eCFR / Office of the Federal Register & GPO

uncertainty_reason: Materiality of the 211.110(c) omission is a judgment, but it is the paragraph that specifically addresses testing and the QCU's role.
